speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Of the 28 non-Budget proposed tax changes, 16 changes are proposed refinements to the income tax regime while the remaining 12 changes are technical amendments to remove obsolete provisions or to provide clarification on the law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: We sought views from the public on the draft Bill from 19 June to 10 July 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) has evaluated the feedback received and, where relevant, taken the suggestions in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: The tax measures have already been debated in this House, but I will highlight the key ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: This will help companies navigate through the economic uncertainty and continue with restructuring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Clauses 39 and 40 of the Bill provide for the change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Second, to ease compliance, taxpayers will be able to claim a tax deduction for the full amount of payments made under Cost Sharing Agreements for qualifying research and development (R&D) projects without the need to provide a cost breakdown from YA2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Clauses 11 and 14 of the Bill provide for the changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Clause 46 of the Bill provides for the change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: I shall now outline two key changes arising from MOF’s periodic review of the tax regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: First, we will require businesses to maintain Transfer Pricing Documentation (TPD).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Transfer Pricing refers to the pricing of transactions among related parties, which, in turn, determines the allocation of profits among these parties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: TPD are records kept by businesses to show that they have priced their transactions with related parties at the equivalent of what they would have transacted with unrelated parties in similar circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: This arm’s length principle is an internationally accepted tax standard.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Since 2006, under the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore's (IRAS’) guidelines, IRAS has been encouraging businesses to maintain TPD.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: With effect from YA2019, businesses will be required to maintain TPD.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Jurisdictions, such as Canada, China, Germany, Korea and the United States (US) also have such requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Requiring businesses to maintain TPD demonstrates our commitment to uphold international standards and ensures that the profits taxed in Singapore are commensurate with the functions, assets and risks undertaken by businesses in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: When transactions between related parties are appropriately priced, profits are correctly attributed to the jurisdictions involved in the transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Domestically, TPD ensures that we are collecting the due taxes which are attributable to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Internationally, TPD serves as useful evidence to other tax authorities, which our businesses can use to show that they have complied with the arm’s length principle for cross-border related party transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: TPD will help our businesses minimise and manage cross-border tax disputes as they go global.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: To limit the compliance burden for smaller businesses, this requirement will apply to businesses only if they have gross revenue exceeding $10 million and significant related party transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: We expect this requirement to apply to fewer than 5% of companies, many of which have already been maintaining TPD.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Clause 21 of the Bill provides for the change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Accordingly, we will increase the maximum amount of tax-exempt voluntary contributions made by employers to employees’ MediSave accounts, and the tax deduction allowable to the employer for these voluntary contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Similarly, for eligible companies that make voluntary contributions to the MediSave accounts of the self-employed persons they work with, we will increase the maximum tax deduction allowable to $2,730.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Self-employed persons will receive tax exemption on such contributions up to the same limit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: These changes for voluntary contributions to the MediSave accounts of employees and self-employed persons are in line with the Government’s efforts to promote portable medical benefits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: All other conditions for granting tax benefits in respect of such voluntary contributions remain unchanged.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Clauses 4, 6 and 10 of the Bill provide for the changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: The remaining legislative changes are mostly technical in nature or relate to improvements in tax administration.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As our Prime Minister mentioned in his National Day Rally speech, Singaporeans live up to the age of 82 on average.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, some of us may also experience an average of eight years of ill-health in old age.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There are a number of reasons that would lead to ill-health.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: While having poor lifestyle choices is a major reason for poor health in old age, some factors are inevitable, such as hereditary conditions or even accidents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As some of these problems can be unexpected, it is important to have sufficient savings in old age in case there is a need for medical services and treatment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This will certainly go a long way to safeguarding the employees’ futures.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is also an attractive staff benefit that serves as a source of motivation for employees.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, while all this sounds good on paper, I wonder how many employers would make such voluntary contributions.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Outreach and awareness could be one way to do so.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As it is, Government schemes like MediShield are complex and not fully understood by all.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Some employers may not even be aware that there is such an option, or they may be dismissive of it as an additional expense.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope more can be done to engage employers on this aspect.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps highlight and showcase those employers who support this scheme, just like what has been done for those employers who support National Service.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   It is a good idea to allow employers to top up their employee's MediSave account voluntarily.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, I wonder how many employers would make such voluntary contributions.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Aside from tax deductions, can we explore other ways to encourage employers to do so?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps some employers may not even know there is such an option.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, this amendment Bill provides the legislative basis for the various tax incentives announced during this year’s Budget Statement.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The first pertains to corporate income tax rebate.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: This measure aims to help businesses cope with the challenges of economic uncertainties and the ongoing economic restructuring.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: In order to upgrade, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) would need capital in different areas.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Recently, I had a chat with a boss in the food and beverage (F&B) and food processing industry.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: He said that in the current business environment, it is not enough to just have tasty food.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: F&B business also need to set up a central kitchen or adopt automated production and compete on who has better selling points, such as a robot chef.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Based on the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry’s (SCCCI's) “Annual Business Survey” this year, amongst the 700-plus respondents, two-thirds indicated that this year’s business revenue remained stable or witnessed slight improvement, compared to last year and 55% said profits were either maintained or increased.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: There are more areas where money is needed than areas from which money can be generated.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, the corporate income tax rebate this time is very timely.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: SMEs can continue to work hard and plough the tax rebate into improving their business processes and uplifting their competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: My second topic is tax deduction to encourage collaboration in R&D.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: With this amendment, the Government will liberalise the tax deduction process for R&D projects involving cost-sharing agreements.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Last year, the SCCCI undertook a study that looked into the innovation efforts of SMEs.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Less than one-third of SMEs committed resources into innovation.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Amongst these, close to 40% rely on their internal resources to innovate.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Between businesses and research institutions, one understands the market, while the other specialises in deep technical research.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Each should play to its own strengths, complement each other and achieve a win-win situation.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, they need to leverage external resources to strengthen their R&D abilities.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that liberalising the tax deduction process for R&D projects will encourage more SMEs to actively collaborate with research institutions.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: In this area, trade associations can play a leading role to encourage their member companies to collaborate on undertaking innovation and R&D.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: For example, the Singapore Food Manufacturers’ Association (SFMA) initiated the “Great Singapore Food Gifts Award” three years ago, encouraging local enterprises to develop innovative food concepts and improve in their creative packaging.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Recently, the SFMA also launched the “Food Innovation Product Award”, enabling food manufacturers and tertiary students to collaborate and co-create new and innovative food products.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: This is a good initiative worthy of being emulated by other trade associations.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: My third topic is specific business hub activities.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The booming development of these industries can also push the development of the other sectors.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The hottest topic these days is the “One Belt, One Road” initiative, the key of which is the interconnectivity of infrastructure, finance and trade.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Being the major transportation, financial and trade hub for the region, coupled with its superior geographic location and favourable tax incentives, Singapore has attracted many foreign businesses and multinational corporations to invest in Singapore and use Singapore as a base to offer their products and services to reach an even larger regional market.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: This is the trend and I hope local companies can grasp these opportunities.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Since local businesses are familiar with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) markets, and have extensive connections, they can, therefore, work with Chinese companies and explore third-party markets together.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: In the new economic order, our local businesses need to leverage on their strengths and incorporate external resources.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: It was with this positioning that our Pioneer Generation successfully created an economic miracle.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Today, we can leverage the same positioning and open new doors for Singapore’s future economy.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The amendments relating to third-party voluntary contributions to the MediSave accounts of private sector employees and self-employed persons (SEPs), is a much-anticipated move.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This is essential for the self-employed persons to build up their MediSave account as well as to encourage companies to make voluntary contribution for their contract employees.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: One of the several concerns that the Labour Movement has on freelancers who are on contract for services is the long-term savings adequacy of these individuals, especially for their medical care and retirement.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: These amendments are timely as we see a gradual statistical increase in self-employed and freelance numbers.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: These will surely encourage employers and companies, especially larger organisations, to help their employees and self-employed professionals, like taxi drivers, insurance agents and freelancers, to build up their MediSave and help these individuals build better safeguards for future healthcare costs.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This is also certainly in line with the Government's move to place greater emphasis on health management and healthcare.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: I, indeed, hope that there will be regular reviews of the adequacy of the long-term MediSave savings and such tax reviews to allow for tax exemption, if required, so as to encourage more of such categories of individuals to top up their MediSave accounts.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This is essential as the healthcare cost continues to rise with the rising demands of an ageing population.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: We cannot afford to put off or delay development in R&D.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Instead, we need to do all we can to encourage such efforts in the hope of making great breakthroughs.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: While I welcome the proposed changes to both corporate and income tax rebates despite and in light of economic uncertainties, I would also like to take this opportunity to suggest further review and consideration of the following.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This would be of great financial relief to those caring for the aged and persons with disability, in addition to the relief that comes from the setting up of the Disability Caregiver Support Centre, as planned in Budget 2017.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, I would like to urge the relevant Ministry to allow for courses not directly related to current employment or profession to be allowed course fee relief for the purpose of them obtaining new skills and embrace lifelong learning for future jobs, future skills and future career.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Thirdly, consider increasing parental relief to better reflect rising cost of care and reduced family size.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Fourthly, working mothers' child relief to be similarly extended to the fathers in recognition of shared parenting responsibility.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: If we are true to the values and culture of shared parenting, then the whole-of-Government policies should demonstrate the essence of cultivating such behaviours, attitudes and values of both parents caring for their children with equal responsibilities, both emotionally and financially, and, thus, the tax structure should also support such values to grow.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, the personal income tax rebates should continue as long as the Government's fiscal position remains strong.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: A review of the corporate income tax rebates will certainly help to offset cost of restructuring which is much needed for industries to transform.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The Income Tax Bill amendment is a timely refresh to our tax administration.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In particular, I would like to support IRAS' push for strengthening regulations on related party transactions.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries are facing tremendous fiscal and economic pressures.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: This pressure results in increased scrutiny over the tax policies from lower tax jurisdictions, or even existing trade agreements.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore today has an excellent reputation as a responsible tax jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Nevertheless, it is important that we stay vigilant.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We must not give others real or perceived reasons to cast doubts on the integrity of our tax system.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Some businesses might get affected with added regulations.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: But I have looked at this Bill's detailed implementation and I am satisfied that it is done in a measured and targeted way.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have a number of clarifications to seek on the application and penalties of the proposed legislative regime.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 34D has been expanded to clarify how IRAS will determine whether transactions are conducted at arm's length.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In practice, such determination may be difficult as there may be different interpretations when applying the principle to specific facts and circumstances of multinational enterprises' operations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There may be legitimate commercial and risk management reasons for conducting business activities within different affiliates.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition to the guidance provided in the TPD Guidelines, will IRAS be providing reasons where it makes the determination that a transaction was not conducted at arm's length?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that to assist companies in complying with the arm's length principle, IRAS has introduced an indicative margin for related party loans obtained or provided from January 2017.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would the Minister also consider prescribing a safe harbour margin for guarantees since, conceptually speaking, returns on guarantee represent the credit risk premium in a borrowing arrangement?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How was the quantum of the fine determined, and how does it compare with similar provisions on reporting requirements?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under the same section, the company as an entity, would be guilty of the offence of failing to meet TPD requirements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Has personal liability for officers of the company been considered as a more effective method for ensuring compliance with TPD requirements?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, the latter act arguably should attract higher culpability because of the element of dishonesty.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would it be appropriate to impose higher penalties for providing false or misleading TPDs to reflect the higher degree of culpability?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister provide some clarification on this?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding the clarifications sought, I stand in support of these amendments which signal Singapore's commitment as a responsible member of the international tax community and deter profit-shifting behaviour that undermines the integrity of the tax system, erodes tax revenues and distorts the incidence of tax burden.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We note the various queries raised by Mr Louis Ng in respect of the TPD requirement.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Singapore subscribes to the international principle that profits should be taxed where the economic activities giving rise to the profits are done.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In line with this, we have adopted the international principle of arm's length pricing in our law.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The arm's length principle is not new to Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Under the Income Tax Act, businesses are required to transact with related parties at arm's length.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The new requirement for businesses to maintain TPD further strengthens the implementation of the arm's length principle by businesses in their tax affairs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The documentation will help them, especially when they venture overseas.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: IRAS already has guidance on how it determines whether transactions are at arm's length.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will continue to revise the guidance periodically in consultation with the industry.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Under the guidance, there are various measures that IRAS has in place to minimise compliance burden for businesses to prepare TPD, such as safe harbour margins.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We also note Mr Louis Ng's suggestion for introducing a new safe harbour margin for guarantees.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: IRAS will take this into account in its periodic review for the transfer pricing guidelines.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The arm's length principle ensures that our tax space is duly protected.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As a responsible international tax jurisdiction, we firmly subscribe to the arm's length principle for cross-border transactions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: While we note Mr Louis Ng's suggestion to impose personal liability on employees for failure to meet the TPD requirement, we will monitor businesses' behaviours first after the implementation of this requirement and evaluate the effectiveness of these penalties.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah had earlier asked how many employers make voluntary contributions to their employees' MediSave account.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Er Dr Lee has also mentioned the need for the Government to engage and encourage employers to voluntarily contribute to employees' MediSave accounts.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We would like to assure Er Dr Lee that the tripartite partners have been encouraging more employers to offer voluntary portable medical benefits through making additional contributions to employees' MediSave accounts.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This was included in the Tripartite Guidelines on Re-employment of Older Employees released in May 2016.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We thank Mr Thomas Chua for his support for the enhanced treatment for R&D Cost-Sharing Agreements and agree with his suggestions that companies could leverage external resources, such as research institutions and trade associations, to strengthen their research capabilities and embark on innovation and R&D activities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We also note Ms Thanaletchimi's suggestions to enhance the various tax relief schemes for individuals as well as to extend the tax rebates for businesses and individuals.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will take the feedback into consideration in the periodic reviews of our income tax policies.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Our income tax reliefs are intended to provide recognition to taxpayers rather than offset the actual expenses incurred by taxpayers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Any revision made to our reliefs will still need to ensure that our income tax regime as a whole remains resilient and progressive.
